_comment: Patches for the client dashboard (pages_original/dashboard.html). The links are rewritten, and the Design Studio link in "My design" gets a plain name. Format: site/patches/README.md

steps.why: rewrite the design-time file names to the pages of the site
My design: name the Design Studio link in plain words (the export says "for advanced users", which puts non-technical visitors off the one tool made for them)
steps.anchor: >Open the full design studio (for advanced users)

steps.why: the profile menu's demo "Sign out" item only went to the home page; it is renamed and marked so that snippets/auth.js can send it to the account page, where signing out and deleting the account are (an anchor on the end of the tag, because the start of it differs between link styles)

PostHog analytics: page views, clicks and forms, and (studio page) the studio's own events, which its browser code sends to window.posthog but its server never gives a key for. The script asks GET /api/analytics, so no key is in the page

sign-in: the header link says Sign in or Account, and a request answered "please sign in" (the session ended) leads to the sign-in page. The script asks GET /api/auth/me, so nothing about the visitor is in the page
phone menu panel: the real logo

phone menu panel: a "Terucon website" section after the project pages, so Materials, Design Studio, Inspiration, Finder and the landing page are two taps away here (this page has its own bottom bar for Home, Design, Price and Menu, so the shared bottom bar is not added)
with: Terucon website

steps.why: footer: the real logo (full lockup) instead of the typed TERUCON INDIA

Saathi (the dashboard's scripted voice helper) is retired: TeruBot (site/brand/terubot.js) is the one assistant of the site. Every button that opened Saathi's tray opens TeruBot instead; the tray's own state (tray, hint) can no longer become true
steps.anchor: openAgent = () => { if (!this.state.tray) this.setState({ tray: true, hint: false, drawer: false }); };
steps.with: openAgent = opts => { this.setState({ hint: false, drawer: false }); try { if (window.TeruBot) window.TeruBot.open(opts); } catch (e) {} };

steps.why: "Tell Saathi about it / Just speak": opens TeruBot with the microphone on
the centre button of the phone bottom bar (below 720 px) opens TeruBot
"What happens next?": opens TeruBot with the question typed in (not sent: the person sends it)
steps.anchor: talkNext = () => { this.openAgent(); this.handle('What should I do next?'); };
steps.with: talkNext = () => this.openAgent({ draft: 'What should I do next?' });

steps.why: "Ask for a change": opens TeruBot with the start of a request typed in
steps.anchor: askChange = () => { this.openAgent(); this.bot('Tell me what you would like to change. For example: “make the walls lighter” or “use more wood”. Tap the mic and speak.'); };
steps.with: askChange = () => this.openAgent({ draft: 'I would like to change my design: ' });

steps.why: "Ask about the price": opens TeruBot with the question typed in. TeruBot is not grounded in this demo project, so the scripted price answer is gone (target C6 is unchanged)
steps.anchor: askPrice = () => { this.openAgent(); const R = this.calc(); this.bot('Your price is about ' + lakh(R.total) + ' for all three rooms, with GST. You pay nothing now. What would you like to know?', [{ label: 'When do I pay?', act: 'say', arg: 'When do I pay?' }, { label: 'Is the price final?', act: 'say', arg: 'Is this price final?' }]); };
steps.with: askPrice = () => this.openAgent({ draft: 'Can you explain the price of my project?' });

steps.why: "Ask to help" under the floor choice: opens TeruBot with the question typed in. The choice buttons of the page itself are unchanged
steps.anchor: askFloor = () => { this.openAgent(); this.bot(this.floorCompare(), [{ label: 'Choose Kota stone', act: 'confirmFloor', arg: 'kota' }, { label: 'Choose Jaisalmer stone', act: 'confirmFloor', arg: 'jais' }]); };
steps.with: askFloor = () => this.openAgent({ draft: 'Which floor is better for my waiting area: Jaisalmer or Kota stone?' });

steps.why: the page used to reopen Saathi's tray (and reserve a margin for it on wide screens) when it had been open on the last visit
steps.with: /* Saathi's tray is gone: nothing to reopen */

steps.why: no "I'm Saathi" tip bubble after 1.6 seconds
steps.with: /* no tip bubble: TeruBot replaced Saathi */

steps.why: Saathi's tray: the markup stays in the template but sits inside an sc-if whose condition no data defines, so the runtime never renders it (a few anchored characters instead of deleting 8 KB of markup)
the closing half of saathi-tray-off
Saathi's round "Ask Saathi" button and its tip bubble (every width but a phone): the same never-rendered condition. This replaces the old fab-lift step that kept that button above the bottom bar
phone bottom bar (below 720 px): the centre mic button keeps its place and now opens TeruBot
phone bottom bar: the label under the centre button
the "How would you like to start?" cards
the "Ask Saathi" card of the help page (the second place is the retired button, which is never rendered)
the floor choice
the price page
the help page's lead line
steps.anchor: Talk to a real person, or ask Saathi. We’re
steps.with: Talk to a real person, or ask TeruBot. We’re

steps.why: the help page's answer to "Can I change my design later?"
steps.anchor: Tell Saathi or Rohan what you want to change.
steps.with: Tell Rohan what you want to change.

steps.why: TeruBot below 720 px: this page has its own 74 px bottom bar whose centre button opens TeruBot, so TeruBot's floating button is not shown there; from 720 px it sits at the bottom right (above the shared bottom bar between 720 and 899 px)
mobile dock for 720-899 px (site/brand/dock.md); hidden below 720 px by the style above
insert:
<style>
/* the shared bottom bar on a small tablet only (720-899 px): below 720 px this page has its own bottom bar and Menu panel,
   which carries the same destinations; above 899 px there is no bar */
@media (max-width: 719px) { .tc-dock { display: none !important; } body::after { display: none !important; } html.tc-dock-on:root { --tc-dock-h: 0px; } }
@media (min-width: 720px) and (max-width: 899px) {
  body::after { display: none !important; }
  .tc-dock-on [data-dash] { padding-bottom: calc(var(--tc-dock-h, 0px) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); }
}
</style>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/brand/dock.css">
<script src="/brand/dock.js" defer></script>

steps.why: the side rail ends above the bottom bar on a small tablet (the bar is 0 px high elsewhere, so nothing changes there), and starts to the right of the chrome's sidebar (0 px on a phone, where the rail is a drawer)
the site chrome (site/brand/chrome.js) replaces the dark top bar: it is not drawn while the chrome is on (its dark-mode switch and its text-size button live in the side rail, see tools-in-rail)
insert:
<style>
/* the site chrome is the one header (site/brand/chrome.md) */
html.tc-chrome-on header[data-screen-label="Top bar"] { display: none !important; }
</style>

steps.why: the side rail starts below the chrome's pill, not below the 72 px top bar that is no longer drawn

the dark top bar is gone (the site chrome replaces it), so its two controls that exist nowhere else move into the side rail, above the project card: the dark-mode switch (same state and handler) and a text-size button that opens the same menu as the old account button (text size, account). Dropped with the bar: the demo project crumb, "Call us" (the tel: placeholder; "Call Rohan" is in the Help view and the drawer), the demo avatar and name

the page lays itself out from the width of the window (breakpoints at 720, 1024 and 1280 px, the rail open by default from 1280). With the chrome's sidebar on the left the room it really has is the window minus the sidebar (--tc-side-w, 0 on a phone), so it asks this function instead
insert: <script>window.__tcvw = function () { var w = document.documentElement.clientWidth || window.innerWidth; var s = 0; try { s = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--tc-side-w')) || 0; } catch (e) {} return w - s; };</script>

steps.why: first width: the room beside the chrome's sidebar
the same on every resize (the chrome sends one when its sidebar is collapsed or expanded)

steps.with: const rs = () => { const w = window.__tcvw ? window.__tcvw() : (document.documentElement.clientWidth || window.innerWidth);
